la:adj:liber.gloss: free, independent, unrestricted, unchecked, unrestrained, licentious
senses: free, independent, unrestricted, unchecked, unrestrained, licentious
la:adj:liber.html:
līber, ĕra, ĕrum (old form, loebesum et loebertatem antiqui dicebant liberum et libertatem. Ita Graeci λοιβὴν et λείβειν, Paul. ex Müll.; cf. 2. Liber), adj.
Gr. root λιφ-, λίπτω, to desire; cf. Sanscr. lub-dhas, desirous; Lat. libet, libido
,
that acts according to his own will and pleasure, is his own master; free, unrestricted, unrestrained, unimpeded, unshackled; independent, frank, open, bold (opp. servus, servilis).
In gen.; constr. absol., with ab, the abl., and poet. also with gen.
Absol.: dictum est ab eruditissimis viris, nisi sapientem liberum esse neminem. Quid est enim libertas? Potestas vivendi ut velis,: an ille mihi liber, cui mulier imperat, cui leges imponit, praescribit, jubet, vetat? etc.,: ad scribendi licentiam liber,: agri immunes ac liberi,: integro animo ac libero causam defendere,unprejudiced, unbiased,: liberi ad causas solutique veniebant,not under obligations, not bribed, § 192; cf.: libera lingua,: cor liberum,: vocem liberam mittere adversus aliquem,: libera verba animi proferre,: judicium

audientium relinquere integrum ac liberum, : aliquid respuere ingenuo liberoque fastidio,: libero tempore, cum soluta nobis est eligendi optio,: tibi uni vexatio direptioque sociorum impunita fuit ac libera,: pars quaestionum vaga et libera et late patens,: liberum arbitrium eis populo Romano permittente,; cf. : mandata,full powers, unlimited authority,; : fenus,unlimited,: custodia, free custody (i. e. confinement to a house or to a town), ; ; v. custodia, II.: legatio, v. legatio: suffragia,the right of voting freely,: locus,free from intruders, undisturbed, secure,; ; : aedes, a free house, free dwelling (assigned to the use of ambassadors of friendly nations during their stay in Rome), ; ; : lectulus,i. e. not shared with a wife,: toga (poet. for virilis toga), a man's (prop. of one who is his own master), : vestis,: libera omnia sibi servare,to reserve to one's self full liberty,.—Comp.: hoc liberiores et solutiores sumus, quod, etc.,: est finitimus oratori poëta, numeris astrictior paulo, verborum licentia liberior,: liberiores litterae,: amicitia remissior esse debet et liberior et dulcior,freer, more unrestrained, more cheerful,: paulo liberior sententia,: liberior in utramque partem disputatio,: fusiores liberioresque numeri,: officia liberiora plenioraque,: (flumina) campo recepta Liberioris aquae,freer, less impeded,; cf.: (Tiberinus) campo liberiore natat,freer, opener,: liberiore frui caelo,freer, opener,.—Sup.: liberrimum hominum genus, comici veteres tradunt, etc.,the frankest, most free-spoken,; cf.: liberrime Lolli,most frank, most ingenuous,: indignatio,.—

Free or exempt from, void of; with ab: Mamertini vacui, expertes, soluti ac liberi fuerunt ab omni sumptu, molestia, munere,; cf.: (consul) solutus a cupiditatibus, liber a delictis,: ab observando homine perverso liber,: liber a tali irrisione Socrates, liber Aristo Chius,: ab omni animi perturbatione liber,; : loca abdita et ab arbitris libera,, B: libera a ferro crura,: animus liber a partibus rei publicae,.—
With abl.: animus omni liber curā et angore,free from, without,: animus religione,: animus cogitationibus aliis,: mens omnibus vitiis,; cf.: liberis odio et gratia mentibus,: omni liber metu,: liber invidia,: equus carcere,.—
With gen. (poet.): liber laborum,: fati gens Lydia,: curarum,. —Comp.: liberior campi,having a wider space,.—(ε) Liberum est, with subject-clause: quam (opinionem) sequi magis probantibus liberum est,it is free, permitted, allowable,; : dies eligere certos liberum erat,.—So in abl. absol.: libero, quid firmaret mutaretve,.
In partic.
Free, in a social point of view, not a slave (opp. servus; also to ingenuus): neque vendendam censes quae libera est,; cf. v. 28: dis habeo gratiam quom aliquot affuerunt liberae, because slaves were not permitted to testify,; opp. ingenuus, free-born: quid ea? ingenuan' an festucā facta e servā liberast?: in jure civili, qui est matre liberā, liber est,; : si neque censu, neque vindictā, nec testamento liber factus est (servus), non est liber,: quae (assentatio) non modo amico, sed ne libero quidem digna est,of a freeman,; : liberorum hominum alii ingenui sunt, alii libertini,; cf. sqq.: ex ancilla et libero jure gentium servus nascitur, ; cf. § 85; sqq.—
Free, in a political point of view; said both of a people not under monarchical rule and of one not in subjection to another people,; cf.: ut ex nimia potentia principum oritur interitus principum, sic hunc nimis liberum populum libertas ipsa servitute afficit,: liber populus,: (Demaratus) vir liber ac fortis,democratic, republican, fond of liberty,: civitates liberae atque immunes,free from service,: provinciae civitatesque liberae,: libera ac foederata oppida,: Roma patrem patriae Ciceronem libera dixit,.—
In a bad sense, esp. with reference to sensual pleasure, unbridled, unchecked, unrestrained, licentious: quam liber harum rerum multarum siet (Juppiter),: adulescens imprudens et liber,; cf.: sit adulescentia liberior,somewhat freer,: amores soluti et liberi,: consuetudo peccandi,.—Hence, adv.: lībĕrē, freely, unrestrictedly, without let or hinderance; frankly, openly, boldly: qui nihil dicit, nihil facit, nihil cogitat denique, nisi libenter ac libere,: animus somno relaxatus solute movetur et libere,: respirare,: constanter et libere (me gessi),: consilium dare,: aliquid magis accusatorie quam libere dixisse,: omnia libere fingimus et impune,: ut ingredi libere (oratio), non ut licenter videatur errare,.— Comp.: liberius vivendi fuit potestas,: loqui,: fortius liberiusque defendere,: liberius si Dixero quid,: maledicere,: longius et liberius exseritur digitus,; cf. : ipsaque tellus Omnia liberius, nullo poscente, ferebat,freely, of itself, spontaneously,.

senses: the inner bark of a tree
la:noun:liber.html:
lĭber, bri, m.
Gr. λέπειν, to peel; λέπος, λεπίς; cf. λοβός
,
the inner bark or rind of a tree.
Lit.
In gen.: obducuntur libro aut cortice trunci,: colligatae libris (arundines),: udoque docent (germen) inolescere libro,: natam libro et silvestri subere clausam,; : quam denso fascia libro,.—
Esp., because the ancients used the bark or rind of trees to write upon; usually the thin rind of the Egyptian papyrus, on which the books of the Greeks and Romans were usually written (v. Dict. of Antiq. p. 587 sq.): antea non fuisse chartarum usum. In palmarum foliis primo scriptitatum, dein quarundam arborum libris,.—Hence,
Transf.
Paper, parchment, or rolls of any substance used to write upon (cf.: charta, membrana): quasi quom in libro scribuntur calamo litterae,.—
Most freq. a book, work, treatise: Demetrii liber de concordia,: quas (sententias) hoc libro exposui,; cf. : dixi in eo libro, quem de rebus rusticis scripsi,: libros pervolutare,: evolvere,: volvere,: legere,: edere,: libri confectio,: tempus ad libros vacuum,: cujus (Platonis) in libris,: in Graecorum libris,: librum, si malus est, nequeo laudare,: actorum libri,the official gazette,; cf. 2, 136; and v. Dict. Antiq. s. v. Acta.—
In partic.
A division of a work a look: tres libri perfecti sunt de Natura Deorum,: hi tres libri (de Officiis),: sermo in novem libros distributus,: dictum est in libro superiore,

sicut superiore libro continetur, : versus de libro Ennii annali sexto,: liber primus, secundus, tertius, etc.,; ; —Sometimes, in this latter case, liber is omitted: in T. Livii primo,: in tertio de Oratore,: legi tuum nuper quartum de Finibus,.—

In relig. or pub. law lang., a religious book, scriptures; a statute - book, code: decemviris adire libros jussis,i. e. the Sibylline books,; ; : se cum legeret libros, recordatum esse, etc.,: ut in libris est Etruscorum,; : caerimoniarum,rituals,.—
A list, catalogue, register, .—
A letter, epistle, ; .—
A rescript, decree (post-Aug.): liber principis severus et tamen moderatus,.

la:verb:libo.html:
lībo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
root λιβ-, λειβω, λοιβή; cf. Līber, delibutus, etc.
,
to take a little from any thing.
Lit.
In gen.: libare gramina dentibus,to crop,.—
In partic.
To take a taste of a thing, to taste: jecur,: pocula Bacchi,: flumina libant Summa leves,to sip,.—
Poet., to touch a thing: cibos digitis,: summam celeri pede libat harenam,: cellulae limen,: oscula alicujus,to kiss,.—
To pour out in honor of a deity, to make a libation of any thing: duo rite mero libans carchesia Baccho,: carchesia patri,: Oceano libemus,: in mensam laticum libavit honorem,: pateris altaria libant,sprinkle,: sepulcrum mei Tlepolemi tuo luminum cruore libabo,—
To pour out or forth: rorem in tempora nati,.—
To pour out as an offering, to offer, dedicate, consecrate: certasque fruges certasque bacas sacerdotes publice libanto,: diis dapes,: uvam,: frugem Cereri,: noluit bibere, sed libavit eam (aquam) Domino,. —Absol., to offer libations: libant diis alienis,: Domino,: cum solemni die Jovi libaretur,.—So poet.: carmen aris,Celso lacrimas libamus adempto,.—
To lessen, diminish, impair by taking away: ergo terra tibi libatur et aucta recrescit,; : virginitatem,: vires,.—
Trop., to take out, cull, extract from any thing (rare but class.): ex variis ingeniis excellentissima quaeque libavimus,; cf. : qui tuo nomini velis ex aliorum laboribus libare laudem,: libandus est etiam ex omni genere urbanitatis facetiarum quidem lepos,: a qua (natura deorum) haustos animos et libatos habemus,: unde (i. e. ex divinitate) omnes animos haustos, aut acceptos, aut libatos haberemus,: neque ea, ut sua, possedisse, sed ut aliena libāsse. .—
To learn something of, acquire superficially: sed eum (informamus) qui quasdam artes haurire, omnes libare debet,

la:noun:libertus.html:
lībertus, a, um, adj.
= liberatus, from libero
,
made free, set free, only as subst., one made free, a freedman, an emancipated person (so called in reference to the manumitter; cf. libertinus, II., and on the several classes of freedmen, v. Sanders ad ).
Lit.
līber-tus, i, m.: tibi servire mavelim Multo, quam alii libertus esse,: nec mihi quidem libertus ullus est,: feci, e servo ut esses libertus mihi,: libertus Cossinii,: Ciceronis libertus : Claudii Caesaris libertus,: servos nostros libertos suos fecisset,; ; ; : patrono in libertum manus injectio sit, ; cf. .—
In fem.: lī-berta, ae (dat. and abl. libertis, ; ), a freedwoman: jam libertā auctus es?: tua,: mea,: matris meae liberta,: Anto niae liberta,: si neque ipsa patrona neque liberta capite deminuta sit,: libertis libertabusque meis,; so esp. freq. in inscriptions: LIBERTIS LIBERTABVSQVE POSTERISQVE EORVM, etc.,; sq.—
Transf., in gen., a freedman, without reference to the manumitter; for the usual libertinus (only in late Lat.): de libertis et eorum liberis, (for which: de libertinis,; ).

la:adj:liberalis.html:
lībĕrālis, e, adj.
1. liber
,
of or belonging to freedom, relating to the freeborn condition of a man.
Lit.: liberalis causa or liberale judicium, a suit concerning a person's freedom, v. sqq.; sqq.: si quisquam hanc liberali caussa manu adsereret,; cf. 5, 2, 68: manu eas adserat liberali causa,: nam ego liberali illam assero causa manu,I formally assert that she is freeborn,: judicium,: liberale conjugium,a marriage between persons of free condition,.—Pleon.: ego te hoc triduom numquam sinam in domo esse, quin ego te liberalem liberem,.—
Transf., befitting a freeman, gentlemanly, noble, noble-minded, honorable, ingenuous, gracious, kind (syn.: generosus, ingenuus).
In gen.: ingenium,; : artes liberales,befitting a freeman,; cf.: liberalia studia accipimus, quae Graeci ἐλευθέρια μαθήματα appellant; rhetores continebuntur, grammatici, geometrae,: hae artes, quibus liberales doctrinae atque ingenuae continerentur, geometria, musica, litterarum cognitio et poëtarum, etc.,; cf.: omnis liberalis et digna homine nobili doctrina,: de artificiis et quaestibus, qui liberales habendi, qui sordidi sint,: liberalissima studia,; 52; : spes liberalioris fortunae,of a higher, more respectable station,: responsum,kind, gracious,; so, liberalibus verbis permulceri, ap. P.—
In partic.
Bountiful, generous, munificent, liberal (syn. munificus): liberales (sunt), qui suis facultatibus aut captos a praedonibus redimunt, aut aes alienum suscipiunt amicorum, etc.,: benefici liberalesque,; cf.: liberalissimi et beneficentissimi,: liberalissimus munificentissimusque,: virtus munifica et liberalis,: largus, beneficus, liberalis,.—*
With gen.: laudis avidi, pecuniae liberales erant,.—
With in and acc.: in omne genus hominum liberalissimus,. —
Of things, plentiful, copious, abundant: largum et liberale viaticum,: potio,: liberalius alimentum,.—
Noble, engaging, beautiful (ante-class.): illarum altera pulcer est et liberalis,: lepidā et liberali formast,; ; : species,; cf.: liberales dicuntur non solum benigni, sed etiam ingenuae formae homines, Paul. ex Müll.—Hence, adv.: lībĕrālĭter, in a manner befitting a freeman, nobly, ingenuously, kindly, courteously, graciously.
In gen.: homo liberaliter educatus,: eruditi,: vivere,: servire,i. e. properly,: respondere,kindly, courteously,: oratione aliquem prosequi,.—
In partic., bountifully, profusely, generously, liberally: benigne ac liberaliter,: large et liberaliter,, § 204: instructus,.—Comp.: vivo paulo liberalius,: nec potui accipi liberalius,: ille (sal) in cibis paulo liberalius aspersus,: ubi liberalius malos odimus,more abundantly, more heartily,.—Sup.: dotem largiri liberalissime,: liberalissime polliceri,.

la:noun:libellus.html:
lĭbellus, i, m.dim.
3. liber
. *
The inner bark of a tree, used for writing-tablets: levis in aridulo malvae descripta libello (carmina), Cinna ap. . —
Transf., a little book, pamphlet, esp. a book written in pages, and not in long rolls: epistulae, quas primus videtur ad paginas et formam memorialis libelli convertisse (opp. transversa charta),.
In gen.: scripsi etiam illud quodam in libello,: in quodam joculari libello,; : quoi dono lepidum novum libellum,: horribilis et sacer,: quicquid hoc libelli est,: libellis eum (Scipionem) palaestraeque operam dare,to books,: nostri farrago libelli,.—Of a single satire, .—
In plur., poet., a bookseller's shop: te (quaesivimus) in omnibus libellis, (dub.; al. labellis); .—
In partic., a writing of any kind.
A memorandumbook, journal, diary: si quid memoriae causā retulit in libellum,: in commentariolis et chirographis et libellis,; ; cf. , 7, 31; 11, 3, 142; 6, 2, 5.—
A memorial: non illi in libellis laudationum decreta miserunt,.—
A petition: Atticus libellum composuit: eum mihi dedit, ut darem Caesari,, A, 4: libellum alicui porrigere,: supplices libelli,: vitem posce libello,: libellos signare, subnotare, to answer petitions: libellos signare,: subnotare libellos,; so, ad libellum rescribere, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 3, 3, 5: libellos agere,to have the charge of answering petitions,: a libellis, the officer charged with receiving petitions: Epaphroditum a libellis capitali poena condemnavit,; : A LIBELLIS ADIVTOR,.—
A note of invitation, to hear a lecture, see a play, etc., a notice, programme: gladiatorum libellos venditare,: domum mutuatur et subsellia conducit et libellos dispergit,: munerarius, the programme of a festival, Treb. .—
A public notification, announcement, placard, handbill: edere per libellos,: libellos Sex. Alfenus, procurator P. Quincti, deicit,tears down the auction handbills,: suspensum amici bonis libellum,: vestitur tota libellis porticus,.—
A letter: (laetitias) in libello hoc opsignato quas tuli pausillulo, (cf. epistulam, v. 26): libellum ipsius habeo in quo, etc.,: ut ex libellis ejus animadverti, Brut. ap. .—
A libel, lampoon, pasquinade (post-Aug.): libellos aut carmina ad infamiam cujuspiam edere,; ; : sparsos de se in Curia famosos libellos,: sive quis ad infamiam alicujus libellum aut carmen scripserit,: injuriam patimur ... famosis libellis,.—
A written accusalion or complaint (post-Aug.): componunt ipsae per se formantque libellos,; .—
A lawyer's brief: quid causidicis praestent magno comites in fasce libelli?.—
An attestation, certificate: significent id libello manu sua subscripto,.

la:noun:libella.gloss: An as (the tenth part of a denarius)
senses: An as (the tenth part of a denarius)
la:noun:libella.html:
lībella, ae, f.dim.
libra
.
An as, a small silver coin, the tenth part of a denarius: nummi denarii decuma libella, quod libram pondo aeris valebat, et erat ex argento parva, Müll.: librales, unde etiam nunc libella dicitur et dupondius, appendebantur asses,; : sunt enim in sestertio libellae decem, singulae viginti, teruncii quadraginta, Volus. Maec. 66.—
In gen.
Prov. for a very small sum of money, as with us a farthing, groat, cent: una libella liber possum fieri,; cf. : tibi libellam argenti numquam credam,: quoi neque libellai spes sit usquam gentium,: quom libella nusquamst, nisi, etc.,: quis Volcatio unam libellam dedisset?.—Hence, ad libellam, i. q. ad assem, to a farthing, to a cent, exactly, .—
In inheritances: ex libella, i. q. ex asse, sole heir: Curius fecit palam te ex libella, me ex teruncio,.—
An instrument for detecting any variation from a perfectly horizontal surface, a level, water-level, plummetline: libella aliqua si ex parti claudicat hilum,: collocare et expolire aliquid ad regulam et libellam,; cf. : structuram (parietis) ad normam et libellam fieri, et ad perpendiculum respondere oportet,: locus qui est ad libellam aequus,quite, perfectly level,

lībum (lībus, m., Nigid. ap. ), i, n.
libo; cf.
,
a cake, pancake of meal, made with milk or oil, and spread with honey, : rustica liba,: adorea liba per herbam Subiciunt epulis,; : plena domus libis venalibus,.—Often used in offerings to the gods: liba absoluta esse et rem divinam paratam,: suum Baccho dicemus honorem, ... et liba feremus,; ; ; : melle pater (Bacchus) fruitur, liboque infusa calenti Jure repertori candida mella damus,: haec te liba, Priape, quot annis Exspectare sat est,. līber, ĕra, ĕrum (old form, loebesum et loebertatem antiqui dicebant liberum et libertatem. Ita Graeci λοιβὴν et λείβειν, Paul. ex Müll.; cf. 2. Liber), adj.
Gr. root λιφ-, λίπτω, to desire; cf. Sanscr. lub-dhas, desirous; Lat. libet, libido
,
that acts according to his own will and pleasure, is his own master; free, unrestricted, unrestrained, unimpeded, unshackled; independent, frank, open, bold (opp. servus, servilis).
In gen.; constr. absol., with ab, the abl., and poet. also with gen.
Absol.: dictum est ab eruditissimis viris, nisi sapientem liberum esse neminem. Quid est enim libertas? Potestas vivendi ut velis,: an ille mihi liber, cui mulier imperat, cui leges imponit, praescribit, jubet, vetat? etc.,: ad scribendi licentiam liber,: agri immunes ac liberi,: integro animo ac libero causam defendere,unprejudiced, unbiased,: liberi ad causas solutique veniebant,not under obligations, not bribed, § 192; cf.: libera lingua,: cor liberum,: vocem liberam mittere adversus aliquem,: libera verba animi proferre,: judicium

audientium relinquere integrum ac liberum, : aliquid respuere ingenuo liberoque fastidio,: libero tempore, cum soluta nobis est eligendi optio,: tibi uni vexatio direptioque sociorum impunita fuit ac libera,: pars quaestionum vaga et libera et late patens,: liberum arbitrium eis populo Romano permittente,; cf. : mandata,full powers, unlimited authority,; : fenus,unlimited,: custodia, free custody (i. e. confinement to a house or to a town), ; ; v. custodia, II.: legatio, v. legatio: suffragia,the right of voting freely,: locus,free from intruders, undisturbed, secure,; ; : aedes, a free house, free dwelling (assigned to the use of ambassadors of friendly nations during their stay in Rome), ; ; : lectulus,i. e. not shared with a wife,: toga (poet. for virilis toga), a man's (prop. of one who is his own master), : vestis,: libera omnia sibi servare,to reserve to one's self full liberty,.—Comp.: hoc liberiores et solutiores sumus, quod, etc.,: est finitimus oratori poëta, numeris astrictior paulo, verborum licentia liberior,: liberiores litterae,: amicitia remissior esse debet et liberior et dulcior,freer, more unrestrained, more cheerful,: paulo liberior sententia,: liberior in utramque partem disputatio,: fusiores liberioresque numeri,: officia liberiora plenioraque,: (flumina) campo recepta Liberioris aquae,freer, less impeded,; cf.: (Tiberinus) campo liberiore natat,freer, opener,: liberiore frui caelo,freer, opener,.—Sup.: liberrimum hominum genus, comici veteres tradunt, etc.,the frankest, most free-spoken,; cf.: liberrime Lolli,most frank, most ingenuous,: indignatio,.—

Free or exempt from, void of; with ab: Mamertini vacui, expertes, soluti ac liberi fuerunt ab omni sumptu, molestia, munere,; cf.: (consul) solutus a cupiditatibus, liber a delictis,: ab observando homine perverso liber,: liber a tali irrisione Socrates, liber Aristo Chius,: ab omni animi perturbatione liber,; : loca abdita et ab arbitris libera,, B: libera a ferro crura,: animus liber a partibus rei publicae,.—
With abl.: animus omni liber curā et angore,free from, without,: animus religione,: animus cogitationibus aliis,: mens omnibus vitiis,; cf.: liberis odio et gratia mentibus,: omni liber metu,: liber invidia,: equus carcere,.—
With gen. (poet.): liber laborum,: fati gens Lydia,: curarum,. —Comp.: liberior campi,having a wider space,.—(ε) Liberum est, with subject-clause: quam (opinionem) sequi magis probantibus liberum est,it is free, permitted, allowable,; : dies eligere certos liberum erat,.—So in abl. absol.: libero, quid firmaret mutaretve,.
In partic.
Free, in a social point of view, not a slave (opp. servus; also to ingenuus): neque vendendam censes quae libera est,; cf. v. 28: dis habeo gratiam quom aliquot affuerunt liberae, because slaves were not permitted to testify,; opp. ingenuus, free-born: quid ea? ingenuan' an festucā facta e servā liberast?: in jure civili, qui est matre liberā, liber est,; : si neque censu, neque vindictā, nec testamento liber factus est (servus), non est liber,: quae (assentatio) non modo amico, sed ne libero quidem digna est,of a freeman,; : liberorum hominum alii ingenui sunt, alii libertini,; cf. sqq.: ex ancilla et libero jure gentium servus nascitur, ; cf. § 85; sqq.—
Free, in a political point of view; said both of a people not under monarchical rule and of one not in subjection to another people,; cf.: ut ex nimia potentia principum oritur interitus principum, sic hunc nimis liberum populum libertas ipsa servitute afficit,: liber populus,: (Demaratus) vir liber ac fortis,democratic, republican, fond of liberty,: civitates liberae atque immunes,free from service,: provinciae civitatesque liberae,: libera ac foederata oppida,: Roma patrem patriae Ciceronem libera dixit,.—
In a bad sense, esp. with reference to sensual pleasure, unbridled, unchecked, unrestrained, licentious: quam liber harum rerum multarum siet (Juppiter),: adulescens imprudens et liber,; cf.: sit adulescentia liberior,somewhat freer,: amores soluti et liberi,: consuetudo peccandi,.—Hence, adv.: lībĕrē, freely, unrestrictedly, without let or hinderance; frankly, openly, boldly: qui nihil dicit, nihil facit, nihil cogitat denique, nisi libenter ac libere,: animus somno relaxatus solute movetur et libere,: respirare,: constanter et libere (me gessi),: consilium dare,: aliquid magis accusatorie quam libere dixisse,: omnia libere fingimus et impune,: ut ingredi libere (oratio), non ut licenter videatur errare,.— Comp.: liberius vivendi fuit potestas,: loqui,: fortius liberiusque defendere,: liberius si Dixero quid,: maledicere,: longius et liberius exseritur digitus,; cf. : ipsaque tellus Omnia liberius, nullo poscente, ferebat,freely, of itself, spontaneously,.

la:noun:libra.html:
lībra, ae, f.
cf. λίτρα; root cli-, clino
,
the Roman pound, of twelve ounces: as erat libra pondus, Müll.: coronam auream libram pondo ex publica pecunia in Capitolio Iovi donum posuit,: mulli binas libras ponderis raro exsuperant,: expende Hannibalem, quot libras in duce summo invenies?: neque argenti in convivio plus pondo quam libras centum inlaturos,: dipondii pondo duas erant libras,.—
Transf.
A measure for liquids: frumenti denos modios et totidem olei libras,.—
A balance, pair of scales: cum in alteram librae lancem animi bona imponebat, in alteram corporis, etc.,; cf. .—
A water-poise, plummet-level, level, line: sin autem locus ... pari libra cum aequore maris est,: libratur

autem dioptris aut libris aquariis aut chorobate, .—Hence, ad libram: alteram navem pluribus aggressus navibus in quibus ad libram fecerat turres, of equal height or of equal weight, .—

Counterpoise, balance: contra flatus quoque pervicax libra Bononiensibus calamis,: aes et libra, v. aes.—
The constellation Libra, The Balance, ; ; : felix aequato genitus sub pondere Librae,.—
Trop., a balance (poet.), : animi cunctantis libra,.

la:noun:liberalitas.html:
lībĕrālĭtas, ātis, f.
1. liber
,
a way of thinking befitting a freeman; a noble, kind, or friendly disposition, noble spirit, kindness, affability.
In gen. (rare): liberalitate liberos retinere satius est, quam metu,: qui ita vivunt, ut eorum probetur fides, liberalitas,kindness,: (L. Cassius) homo, non liberalitate, ut alii, sed ipsa tristitia et severitate popularis,.—
In partic., generosity, liberality (the usual signif. of the word; syn.: bonitas, beneficentia, benignitas): beneficentia, quam eandem vel benignitatem vel liberalitatem appellari licet,: liberalitas ac benignitas,: magnificentia liberalitatis,: ut ea liberalitate utamur, quae prosit amicis, noceat nemini,: quid dicam de pietate in matrem, liberalitate in sorores?: liberalitatis virtutes,: illa quidam catachresis volunt esse, cum ... pro luxuria liberalitas dicitur; a quibus equidem dissentio,.—
Transf. (abstr. pro concr.), a gift, present (post-Aug.): decima parte liberalitatis apud quemque eorum relicta,; : unaque et altera liberalitate locupletavit, id. Vit. Hor.—Plur.: revocatae liberalitates ejus,gifts, grants,: liberalitates Neronis revocandas curavit,.

la:noun:libertas.html:
lībertas (old form, loebertas; v. 1. liber
init.), ātis, f.
1. liber
, the state or condition of a freeman, a being free, freedom, liberty, freedom from restraint or obligation,

free will

, etc.
In gen.: quid est enim libertas? potestas vivendi, ut velis,: ne majorem largiar ei, qui contra dicturus est, libertatem et licentiam,: praecidere sibi libertatem vivendi,: tabella dat populo eam libertatem, ut, quod velint, faciant,: libertas in ridendo, in plorando,: omnium rerum impunitam libertatem tenere,: libertas est naturalis facultas ejus quod cuique facere libet, nisi si quid vi aut jure prohibetur,.—With gen.: feminae omnium rerum libertatem desiderant,fin: testamentorum,: verborum (with licentia figurarum),: dialogorum,: caeli,the open air,.—Poet. with inf sit modo libertas, quae velit ira, loqui, : nec mihi libertas imis freta tollere arenis,.—
In partic.
Civil freedom, liberty, opp. to slavery: Scaevae, servo Q. Crotonis, libertas data est,: alicujus libertati parcere, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 206 Vahl.): omnes homines naturā libertati studere et condicionem servitutis odisse,: patriam et libertatem perdidi,: libertas paenulast tergo tuo,: haruspex his promisit libertatem,: aliquem in libertatem asserere,: petitur puer in libertatem,: libertatis condicio,: favor libertatis,; : libertatem dare,: amittere, sq.—
In plur. (anteand post-class.): tribus non conduci possim libertatibus, Quin, etc.,: pecunias et libertates servis et ante dono datas,: in libertatibus dandis,: libertatium conservandarum causa,: lex (Fufia Caninia) cavet ut libertates servis testamento nominatim dentur,.—
Trop.: se in libertatem vindicare,; cf.: in libertatem vindicati,.—
Political freedom, liberty, or independence of a people not under monarchical rule, or not subject to another people (opp. servitus and dominatus): aut exigendi reges non fuerunt: aut plebi re, non verbo danda libertas,: aliae nationes servitutem pati possunt: populi Romani est propria libertas,; cf. fin.: in optimatium dominatu vix particeps libertatis potest esse multitudo,: et a regum et a patrum dominatione solere in libertatem rem populi vindicari, etc.,: alicui eripere libertatem,: in libertate permanere,: libertatem accipere, recuperare,fin.: plus communi libertati tribuere,: per dolum ac proditionem prope libertas amissa est,: conditor Romanae libertatis,.—
The spirit of liberty, consciousness of freedom: dolor animi, innata libertas, prompta excellensque virtus,: timefacta libertas,.—
Freedom of speech or thought, frankness, boldness, candor (mostly post-Aug.): hoc mihi libertas, hoc pia lingua dedit,: vera de exitu ejus magna cum libertate ominatus est,: quae in aliis libertas est, in aliis licentia vocatur,: affectatores libertatis,; : antiqua comoedia facundissimae libertatis,: vox honestissimae libertatis,: libertas ingenii,.—
Freedom from taxation, exemption: aedium,.—
Personified: Līber-tas, tatis, f., the goddess of Liberty, whose temple on the Aventine Hill was founded by the father of Tiberius Gracchus in the second Punic war; in the atrium of this temple the census-tables were preserved, ; ; ; ; 45, 15; ; ; . A statue of Libertas was erected by Clodius on the site of Cicero's house after it was pulled down, .

la:verb:libero.html:
lībĕro, āvi, ātum, 1 (old form of the
fut. perf. liberasso, ), v. a.
1. liber
, to make or set free, to free, liberate (syn. vindico).
Lit., to release from slavery, to free, manumil: amicas emite, liberate,: liberem ego te?: servos,: sese,: aliquem vindictā liberare,.—
Transf.
In gen., to free, release, extricate, deliver (cf. levo) a person or thing from something (an obligation, debt, difficulty, etc.); constr.: aliquem (aliquid) ab aliqua re, with simple abl.; less freq. with gen.
With personal objects.
With ab: teque item ab eo vindico ac libero,: se a Venere,to release one's self from one's duty to Venus,.—
With abl.: divortio te liberabo incommodis, Poët. ap. : defensionum laboribus senatoriisque muneribus liberatus,: aliquem culpā,: aliquem invidiā,: aliquem suspicione crudelitatis,: aliquem magnā sollicitudine,; cf.: populum metu,: liberatus omni perturbatione animi,: aliquem periculo,: obsidione,: se aere alieno,to pay a debt,.—
With gen.: aliquem culpae,: voti liberari,.—*
With ex: multos ex incommodis pecuniā,.—(ε) With simple acc.: vectigales multos ac stipendiarios liberavit,exempted from taxes,: Volusii liberandi, meum fuit consilium,to release from obligation,: Buthrotios cum Caesar decreto suo liberavisset, viz.,from a division of their lands,, C, 11: amotusque post triumphum abdicatione dictaturae terror et linguam et animos liberaverat hominum,: (debitores) capitis deminutione liberantur,i. e. from debt,—
With inanim. and abstr. objects: eum (mundum) ab omni erratione liberavit,; cf. below, at the end of this number: quorum linguae sic inhaererent, ut loqui non possent, eae scalpello resectae liberarentur,would be set free,: liberare agros, to free or exempt from taxes, : publica liberare,; cf.: liberari omnia Asiae emporia portusque,: liberata vectigalia,: fundum alii obligatum liberare,: liberare fidem,to discharge one's promise, keep one's word,: liberare promissa,to cancel promises, to make them void and of no effect,: nomina,to settle debts,: impensam, to clear or repay expenses, .—Of an abstr. object: divinum animum corpore liberatum cogitatione complecti,.—
In partic.
To absolve or acquit in a court of justice (syn.: absolvo, solvo): aliquem, opp. condemnare,: aliquem crimine aliquo,: liberatur Milo, non eo consilio profectus esse, is acquitted of the charge of having undertaken a journey with the design, etc., : reum a judicibus hoc defensionis modo liberari non posse,.—Very rarely with acc. of the charge: crimen libidinis confessio intemperantiae liberavit,.—
To clear, i. e. to pass, traverse, cross over a place without hinderance (post - Aug.): flumen,; ; : angustias freti,: limen,.—
Templa liberata, freed from buildings that obstructed the view, i. e. having a free prospect, .

senses: to swing, brandish, hurl, cast, fling
la:verb:libro.html:
lībro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
libra
.
To balance, make even, level, to determine a level: aquam, to level water, i. e. to ascertain the fall of water by means of a level, : collocationem libratam indicare, id 8, 6, 1.—Pass. impers.: libratur autem dioptris,.—
Transf., to make even or level: pavimenta,.—
To hold in equilibrium, to poise, balance: terra librata ponderibus,: columnarum turbines ita librati perpenderunt, ut puero circumagente tornarentur,: librati pondera caeli orbe tene medio,.—
To cause to hang or swing, to keep suspended, keep in its place: vela cadunt primo et dubia librantur ab aura,are waved to and fro,: et fluctus supra, vento librante, pependit,: aëris vi suspensam librari medio spatio tellurem,.—
To cause to swing, to swing, sway, brandish, set in motion, hurl, dash, cast, launch, fling, throw: summā telum librabat ab aure,: ferro praefixum robur,: caestus,: tum librat ab aure intorquens jaculum,: dextra libratum fulmen ab aure misit,; ; ; : librata cum sederit glans,: librare se, to balance or poise one's self, to fly: cursum in aëre,: saepe lapillos Tollunt; his sese per inania nubila librant,: haliaeetos librans ex alto sese,: corpus in herba,to stretch one's self out on the grass,: incidentis manus libratur artifici temperamento, : librare iter,to take one's way,.—
Trop.
To make of even weight, to balance, make equal (poet.): orbem horis,: crimina in antithetis,.—
To weigh, ponder, consider (poet. and in post-class. prose): librabat metus,: quae omnia meritorum momenta perpendit, librat, examinat, Naz. Pan. ad Const. 7: praescriptiones, Cod. Th. 8, 4, 26.— Hence, lībrātus, a, um, P. a.
Level, horizontal: aquam non esse libratam, sed sphaeroides habere schema,.—
Poised, balanced, swung, hurled, launched; forcible, powerful: librata cum sederit (glans),: librato magis et certo ictu,violent, powerful,: malleus dextra libratus ab aure,: per nubes aquila librata volatu,. —Comp.: libratior ictus,; cf. .—Hence, * adv.: lībrātē, deliberately: aliquid eligere,.

la:verb:libet.gloss: to be pleasing; to be agreeable
senses: to be pleasing; to be agreeable
la:verb:libet.html:
lĭbet or lŭbet, libuit (lub-) and libitum (lub-) est (in Cic. perh. only in the latter form), 2, v. n. and
impers. (libeo, es, etc., as a personal verb acc. to Caper ap. P.) [Sanscr. root lubh, cupere, desiderare; Gr. root λιφ- in λίπτω, λιψ; cf. Goth. liub-s; Germ. lieb, dear; Lat. līber], it pleases, is pleasing, is agreeable: mihi, I am disposed, I like, I please, I will.— Constr. with nom. of a demonstr. or rel. pronoun, with inf. or a subject-clause as subject, or impers. without a subject, and with or without a dat.
Id (quod) libet (mihi): quod tibi lubet, idem mihi lubet,: facite, quod vobis lubet,: cui facile persuasi, mihi id, quod rogaret, ne licere quidem, non modo non libere,; cf.: sin et poterit Naevius id quod libet et ei libebit quod non licet, quid agendum est?: quodcumque homini accidit libere, posse retur,: ubi peregre, tibi quod libitum fuit, feceris,.—Once in plur.: cetera item, quae cuique libuissent, dilargitus est,.—Without a dat.: rogita quod lubet,: faciat quod lubet,: nihil vident, nisi quod lubet,: si quid lubet,: quae (senectus) efficeret, ut id non liberet quod non oporteret,: illa priorum scribendi, quodcumque animo flagrante liberet, simplicitas,.—
With inf. or a subject-clause, with or without a dat.: concedere aliquantisper hinc mihi intro lubet,: mihi lubet nunc venire Pseudolum,; : Qui lubitumst illi condormiscere? Lu. Oculis, opinor, : non libet mihi deplorare vitam,: quarum (orationum) alteram non libebat mihi scribere,: de quo genere libitum est mihi paulo plura dicere,; ; .—Without a dat.: cum illuc ventum est, ire illinc lubet, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 258 Vahl.); : de C. Gracchi tribunatu quid exspectem non libet augurari,: qui in foro, quicum colloqui libeat, non habeant,: incoharo haec studia, vel non vacabit, vel non libebit,; ; : ultra Sauromatas fugere hinc libet,: libet expectare quis impendat, etc., I should like to see who, etc., .—
Absol., with or without a dat.: ego ibo pro te, si tibi non libet,: ubiquomque libitum erit animo meo,: adi, si libet,; ; : age, age, ut libet,: ut libet, as an expression of assent,; ; ; : Ch. Quid in urbe reptas villice? Ol. Lubet, ; : Pe. Qua fiducia ausus ... dicere? Ep. Libuit, ; cf. .—Hence,
lĭbens (lŭbens; LIBES, Inscr. R. N. 2598 Mommsen), entis, P. a., that does a thing willingly or with readiness, willing, with good will, with pleasure (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: studen hercle audire, nam ted ausculto lubens,: Ph. Complectere. An Facio lubens, : ego illud vero illud feci, ac lubens,; ; : cum totius Italiae concursus facti illius gloriam

libens agnovisset, .—Freq. (esp. in Cic.; Cæs. and Quint. do not use libens as an adj. at all) in the abl. absol.: me, te, etc., and animo libente or libenti, with pleasure, gladly, very willingly: edepol me lubente facies,: me libente eripies mihi hunc errorem,; : libente me vero, Mos. N. cr.: quae (res nostrae) tam libenti senatu laudarentur,: cum Musis nos delectabimus animo aequo, immo vero etiam gaudenti ac libenti,.—Sup.: cunctae praefecturae libentissimis animis eum recipiunt,: illam porticum redemptores statim sunt demoliti libentissimis omnibus,: libentissimis Graecis,: lubentissimo corde atque animo,: fecit animo libentissimo populus Romanus,.—

In partic.: libens or libens merito (abbreviated L. M.), a formula used in paying a vow: Jovi lubens meritoque vitulor,: EX VOTO L. M.,: V. S. L. M., i. e. votum solvit libens merito, or V. L. S., i. e. votum libens solvit, very freq. in inscriptions. —
Transf., glad, happy, joyful, cheerful, merry (ante-class.): uti ego illos lubentiores faciam, quam Lubentia'st,: ego omnes hilaros, lubentes, laetificantes faciam ut fiant,: hilarum ac lubentem fac te in gnati nuptiis,.—Hence, adv.: lĭbenter or lŭbenter, willingly, cheerfully, gladly, with pleasure, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 239 Vahl.); id. ap. (Trag. v. 379 ib.): cenare lubenter,: ecastor frigida non lavi magis lubenter,: ut homines te libenter studioseque audiant,; : libenter verbo utor Catonis,; ; : ego tuas litteras legi libenter,; : libenter homines id, quod volunt, credunt,.—Comp.: ille adjurans, nusquam se umquam libentius (cenavisse),with a better appetite,; : nihil libentius audiunt,; : nil umquam hac carne libentius edit,.—Sup.: cui ego quibuscumque rebus potero libentissime commodabo, ap. : cum lubentissime edis, Favorin. ap. : libentissime dare,; ; .— Hence also,
lĭbĭtus, a, um, P. a.; only plur. as subst.: lĭbĭta, ōrum, n., lit., the things that please, one's pleasure, will, liking, humor (Tacitean): sua libita exercebant,: ad libita Caesarum,: ad libita Pallantis,.

( = libet, ante-class.): est lubido orationem audire,; : est lubido homini suo animo opsequi,; ; —

Sensual desire, lust (the usual meaning in plur.): procreandi,: libidinis ministri,: commiscendorum corporum mirae libidines,: qui voluptatum libidine feruntur,: qui feruntur libidine,: libidine accendi,: mala libido Lucretiae per vim stuprandae,; ; ; : eadem summis pariter minimisque libido,: saltante libidine,i. e. passion goading on,.—Esp., of unnatural lust, ; . —Of unbridled indulgence: vinulentiam ac libidines, grata barbaris, usurpans,.—Hence,

lībertas (old form, loebertas; v. 1. liber
init.), ātis, f.
1. liber
, the state or condition of a freeman, a being free, freedom, liberty, freedom from restraint or obligation,

free will

, etc.
In gen.: quid est enim libertas? potestas vivendi, ut velis,: ne majorem largiar ei, qui contra dicturus est, libertatem et licentiam,: praecidere sibi libertatem vivendi,: tabella dat populo eam libertatem, ut, quod velint, faciant,: libertas in ridendo, in plorando,: omnium rerum impunitam libertatem tenere,: libertas est naturalis facultas ejus quod cuique facere libet, nisi si quid vi aut jure prohibetur,.—With gen.: feminae omnium rerum libertatem desiderant,fin: testamentorum,: verborum (with licentia figurarum),: dialogorum,: caeli,the open air,.—Poet. with inf sit modo libertas, quae velit ira, loqui, : nec mihi libertas imis freta tollere arenis,.—
In partic.
Civil freedom, liberty, opp. to slavery: Scaevae, servo Q. Crotonis, libertas data est,: alicujus libertati parcere, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 206 Vahl.): omnes homines naturā libertati studere et condicionem servitutis odisse,: patriam et libertatem perdidi,: libertas paenulast tergo tuo,: haruspex his promisit libertatem,: aliquem in libertatem asserere,: petitur puer in libertatem,: libertatis condicio,: favor libertatis,; : libertatem dare,: amittere, sq.—
In plur. (anteand post-class.): tribus non conduci possim libertatibus, Quin, etc.,: pecunias et libertates servis et ante dono datas,: in libertatibus dandis,: libertatium conservandarum causa,: lex (Fufia Caninia) cavet ut libertates servis testamento nominatim dentur,.—
Trop.: se in libertatem vindicare,; cf.: in libertatem vindicati,.—
Political freedom, liberty, or independence of a people not under monarchical rule, or not subject to another people (opp. servitus and dominatus): aut exigendi reges non fuerunt: aut plebi re, non verbo danda libertas,: aliae nationes servitutem pati possunt: populi Romani est propria libertas,; cf. fin.: in optimatium dominatu vix particeps libertatis potest esse multitudo,: et a regum et a patrum dominatione solere in libertatem rem populi vindicari, etc.,: alicui eripere libertatem,: in libertate permanere,: libertatem accipere, recuperare,fin.: plus communi libertati tribuere,: per dolum ac proditionem prope libertas amissa est,: conditor Romanae libertatis,.—
The spirit of liberty, consciousness of freedom: dolor animi, innata libertas, prompta excellensque virtus,: timefacta libertas,.—
Freedom of speech or thought, frankness, boldness, candor (mostly post-Aug.): hoc mihi libertas, hoc pia lingua dedit,: vera de exitu ejus magna cum libertate ominatus est,: quae in aliis libertas est, in aliis licentia vocatur,: affectatores libertatis,; : antiqua comoedia facundissimae libertatis,: vox honestissimae libertatis,: libertas ingenii,.—
Freedom from taxation, exemption: aedium,.—
Personified: Līber-tas, tatis, f., the goddess of Liberty, whose temple on the Aventine Hill was founded by the father of Tiberius Gracchus in the second Punic war; in the atrium of this temple the census-tables were preserved, ; ; ; ; 45, 15; ; ; . A statue of Libertas was erected by Clodius on the site of Cicero's house after it was pulled down, .
